newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-ROSSET LIES IN WAIT FOR TOP SEED SAMPRAS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ROSSET LIES IN WAIT FOR TOP SEED SAMPRAS.

text.p: Towering Marc Rosset sneaked into the fourth round of the French Open virtually unnoticed on Friday to set up a likely encounter with world number one Pete Sampras this weekend.

Playing on a sun-drenched centre court, the lanky 1992 Olympic champion completed a low-key 6-3 5-7 6-2 6-3 victory over stubborn Frenchman Lionel Roux, ranked 60th in the world, to bolster a Swiss challenge headed by women's top seed Martina Hingis.

Although hard to overlook at 2.01 metres, Rosset seeded 15th and a semifinalist a year ago, continues to be overshadowed by Hingis, the women's world number one, but his big serve makes him a dangerous customer on most surfaces.
"This was the worst of my three matches so far," said Rosset, a title winner in Antwerp in February. "Nothing against Roux, he's good player, but he's not as good a serve and volleyer.
"I'm just playing two percent better than the other player. That's what happened today. I only played slightly better than I had to. I haven't had the killer instinct."
The win set up a possible meeting with top seed Sampras in the next round. Sampras, however, still has to get by Sweden's Magnus Norman in his third round clash later on Friday.
"If it's Pete Sampras I play then I'll need to be more aggressive," said Rosset. "But I'm not worried, if I play someone better I raise my game."
It was a poor start to what could be an important day for the French with no less than five players, including top men's hope Cedric Pioline trying to find their way into the round of 16.
Pioline, a quarter-finalist last year, will meet defending champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov on centre court in what is expected to be one of the day's more intriguing encounters.
Karina Habsudova of Slovakia meanwhile became only the second women's seed to fall when she crashed out to Romania's Ruxandra Dragomir 6-3 6-2.
Habsudova, seeded 15th and a quarter-finalist last year, joins Germany's Anke Huber, who was seeded eighth, as the only women's casualties.
